Q0393

“Being all equal and independent, no one ought to harm another in…” — John Locke (Q0393)

An English quotation associated with Second Treatise of Government, organized here under justice.

Quotes / John Locke / Q0393

English

Being all equal and independent, no one ought to harm another in his life, health, liberty, or possessions.
Thinker John Locke
School British Empiricism
Source Second Treatise of Government
Theme Justice
Another quotation More from this thinker

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source context

Archive record: this English passage is associated with Second Treatise of Government, within the British Empiricism tradition. Use the cited work or edition when a scholarly attribution is needed.

A short reading

Read in the register of justice, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In John Locke's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
